steps.title: Import React
steps.instruction: Import React from the 'react' package to enable JSX and React components.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring React into your file.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing a library
import React from 'react';
steps.expectedOutcome: React is imported and ready to use.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported React. This allows you to use JSX and React components.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're importing React from the 'react' package.
steps.feedbackWrong: That doesn't look right. You need to import React from 'react'.

steps.title: Create the main component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named App that returns an empty div element.
steps.hint: You can use either a function declaration or an arrow function. Make sure to return a JSX div element.
steps.seedCode:
// Import React here

// Create the App component here
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component is created and returns an empty div.
successCriteria: A functional component named App is defined and returns a JSX div element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the App component that returns a div.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure your component is named App and returns a JSX div element.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component isn't quite right. Check that you've defined a function named App that returns a div element.

steps.title: Add a heading element
steps.instruction: Inside your App component's return statement, add an h1 element with the text 'Inline Styles Demo' inside the existing div.
steps.hint:
Add the h1 element as a child of the div, using JSX syntax:

Inline Styles Demo
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will render a div containing an h1 heading with the text 'Inline Styles Demo'.
successCriteria: The h1 element with text 'Inline Styles Demo' is added inside the div in the App component's return statement.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the heading element to your component structure.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the h1 element has the exact text 'Inline Styles Demo' and is placed inside the div.
steps.feedbackWrong:
The heading element wasn't added correctly. Check that you've added

Inline Styles Demo

inside the div in your return statement.

steps.title: Add a paragraph element
steps.instruction: Inside your component's return statement, add a paragraph element with the text 'This text has inline styles' after the existing heading element.

steps.analogousExample:
// Adding a paragraph element after another element

Title

Some paragraph text
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will display a heading followed by a paragraph with the text 'This text has inline styles'.
successCriteria: A paragraph element with the text 'This text has inline styles' is added after the heading element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added a paragraph element to display text content.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a paragraph element, but make sure it contains exactly the text 'This text has inline styles'.

steps.title: Apply inline style to the heading
steps.instruction: Add a style attribute to the existing h1 element with a JavaScript object that sets the color property to 'darkblue'.
steps.hint: In JSX, the style attribute accepts a JavaScript object where CSS property names are written in camelCase. For example: style={{ color: 'red' }}.
steps.analogousExample:
// Adding inline styles to an element

Styled Heading
steps.expectedOutcome: The heading text should appear in dark blue color when you preview the app.
successCriteria: The h1 element has a style attribute with an object that sets color to 'darkblue'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully applied inline styles to the heading using a JavaScript object.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the style attribute uses a JavaScript object with the correct property name and value.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you added the style attribute to the h1 element with an object like { color: 'darkblue' }.

steps.title: Apply multiple inline styles to the paragraph
steps.instruction: Add a style attribute to the paragraph element with an object that sets fontSize to '18px', fontWeight to 'bold', and color to 'green'.
steps.hint: Use double curly braces for the style object: style={{ fontSize: '18px', fontWeight: 'bold', color: 'green' }}
steps.analogousExample:
// Adding multiple inline styles to an element

Styled text
steps.expectedOutcome: The paragraph element will have three style properties applied: fontSize, fontWeight, and color.
successCriteria: The paragraph element has a style attribute with an object containing fontSize: '18px', fontWeight: 'bold', and color: 'green'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully applied multiple inline styles to the paragraph element using a single style object.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've included all three style properties: fontSize, fontWeight, and color with their correct values.
steps.feedbackWrong: The paragraph element doesn't have the required style properties. Remember to use double curly braces for the style object and include all three properties.

steps.title: Add a button element
steps.instruction: Add a button element with the text 'Click Me' after the paragraph in your component.
steps.hint: Insert a
steps.expectedOutcome: A button with the text 'Click Me' appears after the paragraph in the rendered component.
successCriteria: The button element is added after the paragraph with the correct text content.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the button element.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a button, but check the text content or placement relative to the paragraph.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button element is missing or incorrectly placed. Make sure to add it after the paragraph.

steps.title: Apply dynamic inline style to the button
steps.instruction: Inside your component, create a variable named buttonColor with the value 'red', then use it in the button's style object to set backgroundColor.
steps.hint: Define a variable before the return statement, then reference it inside the style object using curly braces.
steps.expectedOutcome: The button will have a red background color set via a JavaScript variable.
successCriteria: Variable buttonColor is declared with value 'red'
button's style object uses buttonColor for backgroundColor
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully used a JavaScript variable to set a dynamic inline style.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've created the buttonColor variable and used it in the button's style object.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button's background color isn't set dynamically. Check that you created a variable and referenced it correctly.

steps.title: Add a div container with inline styles
steps.instruction: Wrap all existing content inside your component's return statement with a <div> element that has inline styles for padding: '20px', border: '2px solid gray', and borderRadius: '8px'.
steps.hint:
Add an opening
tag before your existing content and a closing
tag after it. Include a style attribute with an object containing the three style properties.
steps.analogousExample:
// Wrapping content in a styled div

Title

Content
steps.expectedOutcome: All content will be wrapped in a div container with gray border, rounded corners, and internal padding.
successCriteria: A div element wraps all existing content and has inline styles for padding: '20px', border: '2px solid gray', and borderRadius: '8px'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully wrapped the content in a styled container. This demonstrates how inline styles can be applied to layout elements for visual grouping.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a div wrapper, but check that it includes all three style properties: padding, border, and borderRadius with the specified values.
steps.feedbackWrong: The content isn't properly wrapped in a div with the required inline styles. Make sure to add a <div> element around all existing content with the style object containing padding, border, and borderRadius.

steps.title: Export the component
steps.instruction: Export the App component as the default export so it can be used in other files.
steps.hint: Add the export statement at the end of your file, after the component definition.
steps.analogousExample:
// Export a component as default
export default MyComponent;
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component will be available for import in other files.
successCriteria: The App component is exported as the default export.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully exported the App component. This makes it available for use in other files.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're exporting the App component as the default export.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check your export statement. You need to export the App component as the default export.
